What is drawn from the plans

Walls, doors, windows, stairs, ramps, room sizes, furniture layout, plumbing fixtures, toilet partitions and the parking lot come straight from the Jeffrey Parker Architects cost-estimating set. Ceiling heights are the ones tagged on the reflected ceiling plans. In the worship center, every chair sits where a chair is drawn, the platform seating follows the plan and section 4/A4.1 (7 inch risers, seven levels on the north-west side, four on the north-east), and the sound booth, baptistry and Viewing 205 are placed from the plan. Exterior materials follow the elevation notes.

Checked against the drawings

Of the 86 dimension strings on the two floor plans, 80 could be traced on the drawing by a checking script. All 80 match their drawn length within a quarter inch. For 76 of them both ends sit on a wall face in the model within three quarters of an inch. The other four run to the middle of a wall or to something that is not a wall. Two more were checked by hand and match. Floor levels, window and storefront heights and parapet heights were checked against the sections and elevations.

What is assumed

The drawings give no heights for the stage, the sound booth or the baptistry. The stage is set at 2'-11" because five risers are drawn at each stair. The sound booth has 3'-6" walls and a one-step operator platform. The baptistry rim is five risers above Back Stage with its viewing opening from 3'-4" to 8'-0", and the opening into Viewing 205 is 9'-0" high. A short stair is assumed where the Back Stage door meets the stage, and steps at the east exit doors. Also assumed: furniture styles and cubicle panel height (about 4'-5"), exposed joist sizes, site grading, landscaping, parked cars, and the outside shape of the existing building. Its worship center is modelled as a 106 by 91 foot box with the lobby under a lower roof on the north side, which is what the ceiling plan and section 4 show at the new platform seating. Existing windows are placed where the plan's wall lines break. The untouched existing rooms on the lower level are laid out from the plan's background lines only.

Colors

Interior colors follow photos of the building as it is today: white walls, black frames and light fixtures, polished concrete in the commons, wood doors, a board-front reception desk like the welcome desk, and the gym's black walls and maple floor. The plans do not call out colors, so treat these as a fair guess.
